headline: An intercepted Riyadh missile, an unconfirmed Yanbu refinery claim and a third straight lower close in crude leave the weekend ledger two-sided, with the venue halted for seven of the 24 published hours and the 22:00Z restart carrying the window's highest allowance
body:
Seven of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME equity-futures weekend halt. The remaining seventeen contain the 22:00Z restart, the Asian session that follows, the European hours into Monday morning and the United States cash open at 13:30Z. Cash equities last traded on Friday 18 September and there has been no live NQ price path since 21:00Z that day.

Every Friday mark was re-verified at primary sources for this run and all are unchanged. The Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% against a previous close of 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 annual high. VIX settled 14.81, down 4.08%, near the low end of a 13.38-35.30 annual range. The Federal Reserve H.15 release for 17 September shows the 2-year at 4.67%, the 10-year at 4.94% and effective fed funds at 3.88%, the last of these 25 basis points above the prior 3.63% after the first policy increase in three years. WTI settled 100.30 and Brent 103.87, a third consecutive lower session.

Two weekend threads point in opposite directions. A Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh was intercepted and destroyed at dawn on Saturday; residents reported an explosion and a plume of smoke near the airport, and Saudi authorities reported no casualties or damage. The Houthis separately claimed strikes on sensitive sites in Riyadh and on an Aramco facility at Yanbu, claims Saudi officials have not confirmed and on which Aramco declined to comment. That unresolved claim is the reason Stress is carried one point higher than the prior hour. Pulling the other way, the East-West pipeline that normally moves 4-5% of global supply is on a reported partial-restart path within days and full capacity in about six weeks, and crude has fallen for three straight sessions.

Tail measures the pathological price path that denies mean reversion, and a closed venue cannot produce one. The published drift from 5 to 18 across the halted hours is a conditional allowance for the reopening print, which absorbs two days of accumulated headlines at once, not a claim that any structure has been observed. It decays through the Asian session on the assumption that discovery is orderly and genuine retracements occur. A second, smaller allowance is carried into the 13:30Z Monday cash open, where aligned opening continuation has historically been a real amplifier. Both remain well inside the EA_ON band, and only observed shallow pullbacks with repeated extension after failed retracements would justify more.

No United States macro release of high impact falls anywhere inside this window. The only scheduled US catalysts in it are the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z and the Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30Z on Monday, both medium impact. The first high-impact release of the week is the S&P Global Flash PMI set on Wednesday 23 September. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was unusable this run: the file was collected at 12:38Z with collectionStatus partial, its calendar and futures sections unavailable and its headline titles empty, so the assessment rests entirely on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green with dominant mode normal, because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure at any point in the window. Tail held 5 through the first seven slots, eased to 4 from 22:00Z Saturday through 04:00Z Sunday and returned to 5 across the final ten slots. Stress rose steadily from 22 to 31 as the Riyadh attack and the unconfirmed Yanbu claim entered the evidence set, while Confidence oscillated in a narrow 72-76 band. The series shows no regime change, only the slow accumulation of unpriced weekend headlines against a closed market.
outlookSummary: Seven of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt; the remaining seventeen contain the 22:00Z restart, the Asian session, the European hours and the Monday United States cash open at 13:30Z. No high-impact United States macro release falls anywhere inside this window, and the only scheduled US catalysts are the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z and the Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30Z on Monday. Tail rises from 5 to a window high of 18 at the restart, decays through the Asian session toward 10, then carries a second allowance to 14 across the cash open. Every published slot maps to EA_ON and no danger window is identified, because both peaks are conditional allowances for structural checkpoints rather than observed one-way structure.
